svg.aria-label: One line from a CI job, cd web and-and TAG equals CI_TAG with a default of dev, semicolon, a subshell that runs cd docs and make, semicolon, npm run build with a tag of dollar TAG, followed through five processing steps. Every row draws the same line at the same coordinates: each segment keeps its column from top to bottom, and the only thing that changes is which cells are dark, meaning this step changed them. A right-hand column lists the state each step leaves behind for the rest of the line. Step A splits the line into four segments on the and-and and the semicolons but not inside the parentheses. Step B follows cd: the first segment moves the working directory from slash ci to slash ci slash web, while the cd inside the parentheses is marked as ending at the closing parenthesis. Step C assigns TAG, which becomes dev because CI_TAG is not set. Step D expands dollar TAG in the last segment, which becomes npm run build dash-dash tag dev. Step E shows where each segment really ran, and the npm segment is outlined: it runs in slash ci slash web, not in the docs directory. Below a dashed rule the same line is run again with CI_TAG set to 2.1.0, and only the two cells that depend on it change. A closing note says the command that actually runs is not written anywhere in the raw line
svg.font-family: Poppins, 'Noto Sans SC', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif

g.text: THE LINE AT THIS POINT · CELLS NEVER MOVE; DARK = CHANGED HERE

svg.text: The command that actually runs, npm run build --tag dev in /ci/web, is not written anywhere in the raw line.
It exists only once the carried state is applied — and the cells stay put so the eye reads one column down instead of re-parsing every row.
